# GopherCon Brief

## Submission Fields (historical, live unverified)

Historical shape from Gopher Academy / PaperCall era; live 2027 field names, limits, voice, selectors vs free text are all UNVERIFIED:

- Title: short, pithy, can be punny/cryptic; avoid BuzzFeed/clickbait ("seatbait"). Cute vague titles punished — attendees pick talks minutes before start. (verified: <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/gophercon-2017/writing-a-successful-gophercon-proposal/> , <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/storytelling-on-stage-the-basics/> , <https://carolynvanslyck.com/blog/2018/12/talk-at-gophercon/>)
- Abstract: historical limit 300 characters; hook + elevator pitch; one sentence topic + one sentence takeaway; state topic and target audience; no teasing. Used on website/agenda. (verified: <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/storytelling-on-stage-the-basics/> , <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/gophercon-2017/writing-a-successful-gophercon-proposal/>)
- Description: long-form; historical floor 200-300 words minimum; thin proposals "rarely chosen over detailed ones". Shape: intro paragraph(s) + outline + conclusion paragraph(s), ideally the actual talk intro/conclusion. Must cover: core topic, target audience, Go-community relevance + "why now", impact/takeaways, why you (experience, not expertise). (verified: <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/storytelling-on-stage-the-basics/> , <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/gophercon-2017/writing-a-successful-gophercon-proposal/> , <https://dave.cheney.net/2017/02/12/how-to-write-a-successful-conference-proposal>)
- Outline: required, with timing per section (ranges + skippable/expandable sections to prove time control). Rule of thumb: 25-min = 1 topic + 1 subtopic; 45-min = 2-3 topics, 1-2 subtopics. (verified: <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/storytelling-on-stage-the-basics/> , <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/storytelling-on-stage-advice/>)
- Reviewer-only notes: disclose everything — best practices recommended, libraries, myths debunked, links to gists/posts, full outline. Reviewers score blind on title/abstract/description only. (verified: <https://carolynvanslyck.com/blog/2018/12/talk-at-gophercon/> , <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/gophercon-2017/writing-a-successful-gophercon-proposal/>)
- Voice (abstract/description person): UNVERIFIED for live CFP. Do not assume third person.
- Selectors vs free text: UNVERIFIED for live CFP.
- Bio: human-owned. Agents never touch it. Customize per talk to highlight relevant background. (verified process: <https://carolynvanslyck.com/blog/2018/12/talk-at-gophercon/>)

## Speaker Constraints on File (2026-10-12, live unverified)

- Eligible main-track format UNVERIFIED for 2027. Historical: 25-min and 45-min talks (verified: <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/storytelling-on-stage-the-basics/>); 2017-era keynotes/tutorials/workshops (verified: <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/gophercon-2017/writing-a-successful-gophercon-proposal/>).
- 2026 had pre-conference workshops + Main Theatre Lightning Talks ≤7 minutes, separate June process (verified: <https://gophercon.com/>). Whether LT counts as CFP format for this brief is UNVERIFIED.
- Include a concrete timed structure matching the chosen slot; reviewers check achievability (no over/under-run, no rambling). (verified: <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/storytelling-on-stage-the-basics/> , <https://dave.cheney.net/2017/02/12/how-to-write-a-successful-conference-proposal>)

## Strictness

Medium-high, story-driven. Odds cited ~10% at review vs ~25% (3 tracks + hallway) at attendance; hundreds of proposals, often 100+ in final 48h. (verified: <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/storytelling-on-stage-storytelling/> , <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/storytelling-on-stage-proposal-writing-for-procrastinators/>)

Reviewers reward (GopherCon-specific):

- Go relevance that fails the substitution test (cannot swap in another language); non-Go topics need explicit "why GopherCon / why now". (verified: <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/gophercon-2017/writing-a-successful-gophercon-proposal/>)
- Experience over expertise: beginner/intermediate first-hand journey accepted; just-in-time learning punished. (verified: <https://carolynvanslyck.com/blog/2018/12/talk-at-gophercon/> , <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/storytelling-on-stage-the-basics/>)
- Story, not reference post: "Why I thought X but did Y", mistakes, what did not go as planned; difficult topics made followable live. Pure "How to do X" belongs in a blog post. (verified: <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/storytelling-on-stage-the-basics/>)
- Proposal as newspaper (front-load the lede, concise-exciting), talk as book (suspense/foreshadowing on stage). No buried lede. (verified: <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/storytelling-on-stage-storytelling/>)
- Tight focus: 1-2 takeaways; small scope covered in depth beats broad survey. (verified: <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/storytelling-on-stage-the-basics/>)
- Novelty: new speakers/angles preferred; resubmits must show feedback incorporated + landscape change. (verified: <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/gophercon-2017/writing-a-successful-gophercon-proposal/>)
- First-hand insight over docs rehash; product case study only with universal lessons, never a sales pitch. (verified: <https://medium.com/@fox/how-to-write-a-successful-conference-proposal-4461509d3e32>)
- Early submit: reviewers gave pre-deadline feedback in 2017 era; last-day submits forfeit it. (verified: <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/gophercon-2017/writing-a-successful-gophercon-proposal/>)

Reviewers punish:

- Rule violations (~30% of proposals in Szczur's sample), sloppy formatting/typos, ableist/shaming language. (verified: <https://medium.com/@fox/how-to-write-a-successful-conference-proposal-4461509d3e32>)
- Selling Go to Gophers ("snow to Eskimos"); assume audience already chose Go, inspire them to convince others. (verified: <https://dave.cheney.net/2017/02/12/how-to-write-a-successful-conference-proposal> , <https://blog.gopheracademy.com/gophercon-2017/writing-a-successful-gophercon-proposal/>)
- Vague/cute titles, teasing abstracts, detail-free descriptions. (verified above)

General craft (incident-first, linear chain, takeaways) intentionally excluded — belongs in agent definitions.
